title: SecB Skill Package Descriptor
description: The AUTHORED tier of a skill manifest (ADR-0013). Every field here is one a package author legitimately holds. It carries no scope, no status, and no approval history: those are grants, and a grant an author can write is not a grant. See skill-grant-record.schema.json for the granted tier, joined on skill_id + version.

package_name.description: The identity binding key. MUST equal the package directory name. The hub denies DENY_IDENTITY_MISMATCH when a resolved grant does not name the directory it was found in, so this field is filesystem-bound on purpose - display_name exists precisely so a human label cannot be mistaken for an authorization join key.

risk_class.description: A process input consumed by the promotion pipeline to select review gates, not by resolution. An author proposes it; review may raise it. Self-downgrade is prohibited by docs/16-security/02-risk-and-mutation-classes.md.

authority_ceiling_cap.description: A CAP, never a grant. A skill never confers authority. Effective ceiling is min(agent_ceiling, skill_cap), composed in exactly one place. Named _cap rather than authority_ceiling so it cannot be confused with the identically-enumerated field on agent-registration.

owner.description: Optional at descriptor stage, REQUIRED before promotion. Not derivable from a package, and intake must not fabricate it (FR-SKI-004).

source.description: licence is optional here and required before promotion, for the same reason as owner.

content_digest.description: Reserved for resolution-time content verification (DEF-B1, DEF-C2). Not yet consumed; the control belongs to Phase 5.

controls.description: The enforceable safety properties. mutation_class is deliberately absent: it duplicated repository_mutation and declared six values while admitting and observing exactly one (ADR-0013).

evaluation.description: DECLARED suites, distinct from executed results. Results live in the grant record's evidence_refs; conflating the two would let a declaration count as evidence.
